title: Token boundary regression guard and template sanity checker for model onboarding
creator: Asha Raman
description: During recent onboarding of several open models we observed intermittent tokenization mismatches between the tokenizer used by the model manifest and the runtime tokenizer shim. Symptoms include off-by-one token counts for system role prefixes, truncated chat messages when using new templates, and occasional KV cache misalignment leading to incorrect continuations at 2-5% in smoke tests. This ticket implements a regression guard and automated sanity checks that run as part of the onboarding pipeline to prevent models with incompatible tokenizer+template combos from being published with a performance profile. The goal is to catch and surface deterministic tokenizer/template incompatibilities early, provide remediation guidance, and ensure the published performance profile corresponds to the runtime tokenizer semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline includes a token boundary regression guard that runs a fixed set of tokenization smoke tests (system role prefixes, role delimiters, empty messages, long sequences)

Template sanity checker validates that chat templates used in the model manifest produce identical token boundaries when run through the runtime tokenizer shim and the model's reference tokenizer (golden diff below threshold)
If a mismatch exceeds thresholds, onboarding fails and a human-readable report is attached to the model manifest with suggested template/manifest edits
Published performance profile includes a tokenizer_version field and pin metadata, and profile publishing is idempotent (retries do not duplicate profiles)
Unit and integration tests cover at least three failing real-world cases previously observed in production (links in comments)
steps_to_reproduce: Pick a model manifest with custom role delimiters (e.g., '<<SYS>>' style) and a corresponding tokenizer manifest that tokenizes delimiters differently
Create an onboarding job that publishes a performance profile without running the sanity checker
Run generation flows using the runtime with the published profile; observe shifted token indices in logs and occasional truncation when prefix tokens exceed batch limits
Run the new token boundary checker and observe the mismatch report and suggested fixes
proposed_solution: Add a new onboarding pipeline stage 'tokenizer-template-sanity' that runs in CI alongside weight checks and perf tests

Implement a lightweight harness that runs pairs of tokenizers (runtime shim vs reference) on curated prompt/template sets and computes a deterministic diff metric: token_count_delta, boundary_mismatch_positions, and first-mismatch-hash
Define thresholds: token_count_delta <= 1 for role-prefixed messages, boundary_mismatch_positions must be empty for the first 256 tokens unless model-specific allowance exists
Auto-generate remediation suggestions: normalize delimiters, fallback to standard chat wrapper, or pin a compatible tokenizer shim version in model metadata
Record tokenizer_version and template_checksum into the performance profile and make profile publishing transactional with a uniqueness key (model_id + manifest_checksum + tokenizer_version)
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement harness and add unit tests; run locally against known failing models (no blocking)
Week 2: wire harness into onboarding pipeline in canary mode (reports only) and run across nightly onboarding jobs for 48 hours
Week 3: enable gating for non-admin manifests; require PM/ML review to bypass
Week 4: full enforcement for all new manifests and retro-run checks for published profiles older than 30 days (generate remediation tickets)
Post-rollout: add a console view for tokenizer compatibility reports and a 'resolve with suggestion' workflow for Solutions Engineers
testing_plan: Unit tests for harness components (token_count_delta, mismatch detection, checksums)
Integration tests against synthetic templates: role-prefixed, multi-line system messages, nested code blocks, and empty assistant messages
Golden diff tests using archived failing manifests (refer to links) — these must fail under current behavior and pass after fixes
Load test of the onboarding pipeline stage to ensure latency adds <5s per manifest on average
QA checklist for Solutions Engineering: reproduce mismatch, apply suggested fix, confirm runtime generation matches reference
